triage.diagnosis: The planner did its job and the run died afterwards. A complete 26 KB work-order.json for #72 — every required field present, four concrete file edits, six acceptance criteria, all four target files real in this tree — was written by the agent and survives in artifact plan-output (id 10896660480) of run 36210315752, 30-day retention. What failed was not the planning. The claude-code-action step logged "Claude Code initialized" at 02:01:25 and then emitted nothing for the remaining 45 minutes, until the hang detector at .github/workflows/sdlc-plan.yml:271 (timeout-minutes: 45, which that file itself calls a hang detector set "far above any honest run") killed it. At job cleanup the SDK's own processes were still alive and had to be terminated as orphans (bun pid 2472, claude pid 2577), so the run was blocked on an unanswered request to the OpenCode Go gateway (https://opencode.ai/zen/go, bridged=false) rather than having crashed: no application code in this repository threw, there is no stack trace, no 429 or 529, no OOM, and runtime.max_turns is empty so nothing capped it from the inside. The stall itself is transient and a plain rerun would probably plan again and finish. I am not rerunning, because the plan this run paid for is real and no verdict can recover it. `resume` re-enters the same stage and only skips work when ledger.approved_work_order is set (.sdlc/bin/plan-strategy.mjs:70), which requires the gate job to have validated and stashed it first — and the gate job admits the plan-output artifact only when needs.plan.result == 'success' (sdlc-plan.yml:567, and the job's own if at 529-533). This run's plan job went red, so the work order was never validated, never stashed and never posted. A rerun would spend another 45 minutes of planner to produce a second copy of a plan that already exists; a resume would post "resuming, not redoing" and then redo it, which is the lie this stage exists to stop telling. So a person decides whether to seed #72's plan from the artifact, and the plumbing gap that throws away a written plan is fixed so the next one is not lost.

Then failed-run.log:1054-1055, ##[error]The action has timed out. at 02:46:25.0121231Z with duration_ms=2709959 — no line from that step in between. failed-run.log:1133-1134, "Terminate orphan process: pid (2472) (bun)" and "pid (2577) (claude)", so the SDK was blocked, not exited. The surviving work: gh api repos/Shivam-Fl/autonomous-growth-os/actions/artifacts/10896660480/zip yields work-order.json (26736 bytes) and plan/brief.md (147 bytes); the work order has issue, version, understanding, approach, files, tests, acceptance, qa_script and the optionals kind/mode/confidence/reproduced/root_cause/risks/out_of_scope/alternatives_considered, no missing required key and no field outside the schema's allowed set, and its four files[] paths all exist in this checkout. Why nothing consumes it: .github/workflows/sdlc-plan.yml:567 downloads plan-output only "if: needs.plan.result == 'success'", and lines 529-533 apply the same condition to the whole gate job, so both were skipped; "Hand over the plan" (sdlc-plan.yml:506-517, if: always()) is what preserved the file. prepare's plan-inputs artifact was a single 147-byte brief.md, so this was attempt 1 with no prior plan and no previous-output.json to correct. failure-packet.json: prior_signatures is empty and occurrences is 1.

framework_defect.what: A plan the agent actually wrote is thrown away whenever its own step goes red afterwards. The gate job's condition (lines 529-533) admits only needs.plan.result of success or skipped, and the plan-output download inside it (line 567) repeats "if: needs.plan.result == 'success'", so a hung or crashed agent step that had already written a complete work-order.json leaves the file in the run artifact and nowhere else: no validation, no ledger entry, no gate, no reviewer. The step that would have kept it, "Keep the validated plan" (616-626), lives in the gate job, so the hang destroyed the plan that run had finished. .sdlc/bin/plan-strategy.mjs:70 then has nothing to resume from, and apply-triage.mjs sends both rerun and resume down the same rerunTarget path, so no verdict a triage agent can legally return recovers the work — the next identical hang loses the same 45 minutes of planning. This run is the case: work-order.json, 26736 bytes, complete and valid, sitting in artifact 10896660480 while the issue is treated as never planned.
framework_defect.fix: In the plan workflow's gate job, stop conditioning recovery on the step having been green. Let gate's if (lines 529-533) also admit needs.plan.result == 'failure' for a plan-mode run, and change the plan-output download at line 567 to "if: always() && needs.plan.result != 'skipped'" so it is attempted whatever the plan job did, keeping its existing continue-on-error so a run that wrote nothing still validates as a missing file by name rather than a failed download. The take-what-was-asked-for copy loop, the transcript recovery, the schema check, the split-criteria check and the reserved-path check already tolerate absence, and keeping a plan on the ledger still does not post or implement it — the gate and the reviewer run over it afterwards, unchanged. The same one-line relaxation is needed on the arbiter's transcript step (498-501) and on the single agent's (352-355), where "steps.fw_single.outcome == 'success'" never holds because fw_single inherits the job's implicit success() and is skipped the moment the agent step fails; key those on the agent step's own outcome ("always() && steps.plan_single.outcome != 'skipped'") so the summary is taken from the execution file even on a timeout. Add a regression test under tests/ that drives a plan job whose agent step fails after writing a work order and asserts the ledger still holds it. Keep every added and removed line clear of the sensitive patterns in .sdlc/bin/lib/self-fix.js — this change must not touch a line naming a token, a permission, a gate or an approval.
